text:
Kasperi Kapanen's top speed this season, 24.05 mph, sits at the very top of NHL EDGE's charts, and Edmonton has given that speed a real job: 18:11 a night, with a spot on the power play.

That second part is where the points are. Seven of his ten have come with the man advantage, including the power-play goal against Anaheim on Nov. 5, the same night he fought. At five-on-five the picture is ordinary. The Oilers take 49% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, about what they do without him, and Evolving-Hockey had him in the bottom 5% of forwards for offense created last season.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking does credit him with something useful: 80% of his zone exits kept possession last season, so his shifts rarely get stuck in the defensive end.

He's shooting 17.2%, above our range for him, so a goal pace near 20 needs the power play to stay generous. The question for Edmonton is whether that role is his because of what he does or because of who he's next to.
